newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey unit in Philippines telecomms deal.
newsitem.headline: Plessey unit in Philippines telecomms deal.

text.p: South African telecommunications and electrical firm Plessey Corp Ltd said on Monday that its AWA Plessey unit signed a 67 million rand telecommunications contract in the Philippines.

"It's for digital equipment and the partner is the Philippines Long Distance Telephone Company," group chief executive John Temple told Reuters, but added that it was still too early to give further details.
Speaking at an analysts' presentation, Temple said the investment was part of projects managed by Sydney-based unit Plessey Asia Pacific which traded as AWA Plessey.
He did not say when the deal had been signed.
He said he was confident the year ahead would present good growth opportunities for Plessey.
The telecommunications market in South Africa was huge, creating many opportunities. Also, the group's operations in the Pacific Rim had opened exciting and growing markets.

In addition to the Philippines contract, AWA Plessey had extended a traffic systems contract in Hong Kong by 10 million rand and had prospects of a traffic systems contract in Manila as well as a new project in Malaysia.
"It's a year of huge opportunity and we as management must make sure that that opportunity comes to Plessey," Temple said.
Positive factors included the disposal of loss-making consumer electronics division TEK to Omega Holdings Ltd for 75 million rand late last month.
Temple said the available cash would be used to eliminate interest charges and would allow for more flexibility in new investments.

Concerns for the year ahead centred on government's industrial policy and the uncertain impact of state utility Telkom's conflicting requirements after its partial privatisation when it comes under new management.
Plessey last week reported a fall in diluted earnings per share for the year ended March to 28.0 cents a share from 40.6 cents before but managed to hold the dividend steady at 13.0 cents.
